## Process

To generate simulation data I did the following for each study $j$ in our empirical dataset:

1) Load the statistics from describe_clusterRCT.  Call these $\theta_j$.
2) Repeatedly, for runs $r = 1, \ldots, R$, generated a dataset with similar characteristics to $j$. I then stored the set of estimates from applying all our estimators to the data.
3) I then calculated the range of estimates for each estimator, and the ratio of the largest to smallest standard error.  I did this both overall, and within each estimand (Person or Cluster).
4) I finally saved the set of results to a file. 

In all of the generated data there were no treatment effects, and no correlations of anything to anything else.  We are looking at a simple scenario.
The block and cluster sizes, number of blocks, and ICC values were all matched to those estimated/observed.

Once done, I loaded all the runs for all the datasets, and then for each run id $r$, I made a histogram of the ranges across all the datasets, mimicing our core figures from the empirical paper.
I also insert the real estimated values as an "imposter" so we could see if the estimated distributions looked like the actual one.

These are in the provided fingerprint figures.


## Results

The two "imposter" plots described above are the following 


```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, out.width="100%"}
aterange_plot
seratio_plot
```

## Aggregate statistics

For each run, we can look at the mean and standard deviation of the ranges of estimates across the datasets in that run.

```{r}


ggplot( ranges, aes( mn_rngATE, fill = real ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Estimand ) +
  geom_dotplot( method="histodot", stackgroups=TRUE, binwidth = 0.005 ) +
  labs( title="Average of the range of estimates across datasets" )

ggplot( ranges, aes( mn_ratSE, fill = real ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Estimand ) +
  geom_dotplot( method="histodot", stackgroups=TRUE, binwidth = 0.05 ) +
  labs( title="Average of the ratio of SE estimates across datasets" )

```
